patch_description:
Restructure the EPLB algorithm as a NumPy-based pipeline, replacing the slow per-layer, per-item Python loops (the O(layers × experts × packs) scans in `balanced_packing` and the repeated full-tensor reductions in `replicate_experts`) with operations vectorized across all layers simultaneously.

Key structural changes:
1. **Batched greedy packing**: instead of looping layer-by-layer and item-by-item with a `min()` scan over packs, `balanced_packing` now processes all layers in lockstep — one vectorized `argmin` over a `[layers, packs]` load matrix per sorted item — preserving the exact LPT-with-cardinality greedy semantics (including tie-breaking by lowest pack index) at a fraction of the cost.
2. **Incremental replication**: `replicate_experts` maintains a running `weight/count` ratio matrix, updating only the selected expert's ratio each iteration instead of recomputing the full division and max over all experts.
3. **Unified NumPy dataflow**: all intermediate permutation/gather/scatter steps of the hierarchical policy run on NumPy arrays (via `np.take_along_axis` and row-wise scatter inverse permutations), avoiding per-op PyTorch dispatch overhead; results convert back to torch int64 tensors only at the entry-point boundary.

The outputs (physical_to_logical_map, logical_to_physical_map, expert_count) are identical in shape, dtype, and semantics to the original, but the algorithm runtime drops from quadratic-in-items Python loops to compact vectorized passes, improving the speed score while keeping the same greedy balancing quality.
